First, we rewrite the integral as

$$
\int (5x-50)^{1/2}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Now, we let $u=5x-50.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=5\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{5}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5x-50)^{1/2}\,\text{d}x & =\int {u}^{1/2}\cdot (\frac{1}{5})\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\int {u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot \frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2}+C \\  & =\frac{2}{15}{u}^{3/2}+C \\  & =\frac{2}{15}(5x-50)^{3/2}+C \\  & =\frac{2}{15}\sqrt{(5x-50)^{3}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\frac{2}{15}\sqrt{(5x-50)^{3}}+C] & =\frac{2}{15}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\sqrt{(5x-50)^{3}}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =\frac{2}{15}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[(5x-50)^{3/2}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =\frac{2}{15}\cdot \frac{3}{2}(5x-50)^{1/2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5x-50)+0 \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(5x-50)^{1/2}\cdot 5 \\  & =(5x-50)^{1/2} \\  & =\sqrt{5x-50}\,✓\end{aligned}
